coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: This story demonstrates strong collaborative value across both pipeline runs. The prior openspec pass established a solid structural foundation; the targeted speckit pass successfully addressed the two flagged gaps from the previous coordinator review (scripts.start/test content values now explicitly verified, and the vitest CommonJS import error root cause is documented and mitigated via the test.include pattern). The split into SKY-001-A (structure/config) and SKY-001-B (verification/validation) is logically clean — no AC appears in both children, and the split boundary is meaningful (static artifact assertions vs. runtime execution assertions). All 21 ACs in the parent are precise, independently testable, and non-overlapping. The one previously flagged gap — missing prerequisite AC for the node20 binary path — remains technically unaddressed as a standalone AC, but the executable verification steps now use fully-qualified paths (e.g. ~/.nvm/versions/node/v20.20.0/bin/node) which implicitly bake in the prerequisite assumption. This is acceptable for an approved story but worth noting: if the nvm path is absent at execution time, the verification gate will fail with a path-not-found error rather than a clear prerequisite message. SKY-001-B adds a valuable fifth AC (vitest CommonJS error absence) that was not present in the parent's AC list — this is a minor inconsistency between parent and child but the child AC is strictly additive and correct. Security coverage is thorough: .gitignore secret-free check, no SDK dependencies, no hardcoded credentials in config files. Overall quality is high and the story is implementation-ready.

stories.title: API Discovery: Verify and Document Skyscanner RapidAPI Contract
stories.description: Before implementing the Skyscanner client, discover and document the real RapidAPI endpoint contract. Using the RAPIDAPI_KEY environment variable, make live curl probes (via the Bash tool only — FetchUrl and WebSearch are prohibited) against the subscribed Skyscanner host to identify: (1) the correct x-rapidapi-host value, (2) working endpoint paths for flight search (one-way and/or roundtrip), (3) required query parameters with exact names and value formats, and (4) the response JSON shape including top-level keys and nested field names relevant to FlightResult. Write the discovered contract to /tmp/skyscanner-app/docs/api-contract.md. This file is the authoritative reference for SKY-002 (client implementation). Probe with `curl -si` so both status codes and response bodies are captured. A 429 (Too Many Requests) confirms a path is valid even when no 2xx body is obtained. Do NOT write any TypeScript, JavaScript, or compiled output in this story.
acceptanceCriteria: /tmp/skyscanner-app/docs/ directory exists and /tmp/skyscanner-app/docs/api-contract.md is present and non-empty.

The probe sequence is executed in order: (1) `mkdir -p /tmp/skyscanner-app/docs`, (2) two or more `curl -si` probes against candidate endpoints on skyscanner.p.rapidapi.com, (3) write api-contract.md with all required sections — no section may be written before the relevant probes have been run.

api-contract.md contains a 'Host' section documenting the confirmed x-rapidapi-host value (must be skyscanner.p.rapidapi.com) with the observed HTTP status code of the confirming probe; a 429 response is sufficient proof of an active subscription.

api-contract.md documents at least one working endpoint path under an 'Endpoints' section; a path is considered working if the probe returned 2xx or 429 — any path returning 404 must not be listed as working; paths on sky-scanner3.p.rapidapi.com must not appear anywhere in the document.
Each entry in the 'Endpoints' section includes the HTTP method (e.g. GET, POST), the full path, and the observed status code from the probe.

api-contract.md documents query parameters under a 'Query Parameters' section with exact parameter names, expected value types, and at least one concrete example value (e.g. IATA airport codes, ISO 8601 date strings).

The 'Query Parameters' section explicitly distinguishes required parameters from optional ones — parameters whose absence causes a 4xx response are marked 'required'; all others are marked 'optional'; the basis for each classification (observed probe result or inferred from documentation) must be stated.
api-contract.md documents required HTTP headers under an 'Authentication' section — at minimum x-rapidapi-key and x-rapidapi-host — plus any additional headers observed in probe responses.

The 'Authentication' section uses only a placeholder value for x-rapidapi-key (e.g. '$RAPIDAPI_KEY' or '<RAPIDAPI_KEY>'); the literal value of the RAPIDAPI_KEY environment variable, or any substring of it longer than 4 characters, must not appear anywhere in api-contract.md.

api-contract.md includes at least one complete, reproducible curl command example targeting a documented working endpoint, with the key shown only as '$RAPIDAPI_KEY' or '<RAPIDAPI_KEY>', such that SKY-002 implementers can re-run it verbatim to reproduce the discovery.

api-contract.md includes a 'Sample Response' section. If a live 2xx body was captured, the section must contain a valid, parseable JSON snippet showing the top-level response structure and at least one flight result object. If only 429 responses were received, the section must include the raw 429 error body and an explicit note stating 'Flight result shape inferred from available documentation — no live 2xx response was obtained.'

api-contract.md contains a 'FlightResult Field Mapping' section that maps each API response field to its FlightResult counterpart (price, origin, destination, departureTime, arrivalTime, carrier, durationMinutes) or explicitly marks it as 'absent' or 'derived'; any field mapping not confirmed by a live 2xx response must be individually marked '(inferred)'.

api-contract.md includes a note explaining that HTTP 429 means the endpoint path is valid but the request was rate-limited; if a Retry-After header was observed in any probe response, its value and semantics must be documented.

api-contract.md includes a 'Discovery Metadata' section containing: the ISO 8601 date the probes were run, the tool used (curl with version if obtainable), and a table or list of every host+path probed with the HTTP status code observed — this section must be structured such that each row/entry is unambiguously parseable (e.g. a Markdown table or a bullet list with consistent formatting).
No TypeScript, JavaScript, compiled output, package.json, lockfiles, or any dependency manifest files are created or modified as part of this story.

api-contract.md must not contain sensitive information such as actual API keys, tokens, or passwords; a final automated or manual scan of the file must confirm no string matching the pattern of the RAPIDAPI_KEY value (or any prefix/suffix longer than 4 characters) is present.

All documented API paths conform to RESTful conventions where applicable — HTTP verbs are used semantically (GET for retrieval, POST for submission), and paths use predictable, noun-based resource naming without redundant or ambiguous segments.

technicalNotes.notes: CRITICAL: Use your Bash tool to run curl commands directly. Do NOT use FetchUrl, WebSearch, or any web browsing tool. Do NOT look up external documentation. Run curl -si probes immediately using the Bash tool. RAPIDAPI_KEY is available in the environment. Known candidate host: skyscanner.p.rapidapi.com (429 responses confirm subscription active). sky-scanner3.p.rapidapi.com returns 404 — do not use it. A 429 (Too Many Requests) on an endpoint confirms the path is valid — document it. The goal is an accurate contract doc, not a working implementation. Probe sequence: (1) mkdir -p /tmp/skyscanner-app/docs, (2) run 2-3 curl -si probes to candidate endpoints, (3) write /tmp/skyscanner-app/docs/api-contract.md with all required sections.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: The speckit agent made genuine improvements over the openspec baseline — tightening key-exposure validation (substring >4 chars threshold), adding an ordering constraint on the probe sequence, requiring the Discovery Metadata section to be machine-parseable, clarifying the 429 Sample Response handling, and hardening the Endpoints section to exclude sky-scanner3 paths from the document entirely (not just the section). These are non-trivial improvements. However, the two directed fixes explicitly assigned in coordinatorNotes were again not applied in this pass: (1) the RAPIDAPI_KEY non-empty prerequisite gate AC is still absent — without it, an agent executing this story with an empty or missing key will run curl probes that silently return 401/403 or fail outright, and all downstream ACs (Host confirmation, working endpoint, Sample Response, FlightResult mapping) become vacuously passable or silently blocked; (2) the inferred contract risk flag from the prior review was acknowledged in coordinatorNotes but the speckit agent's response was structural refinement of epistemic marking rather than a human-confirmation gate. The acAdded list shows that speckit essentially replaced all prior ACs with refined versions rather than adding the two directed items on top — this is a pattern of comprehensive rewrite rather than targeted fix application. The 17 final ACs are individually well-formed, testable, and non-overlapping. The RESTful conventions AC (last item) is slightly weaker than the rest — 'where applicable' is subjective and not independently verifiable without a defined rubric. No story split was performed; the scope is appropriately bounded to a single discovery artifact, so this decision is correct. Human review is required to: (a) explicitly accept or reject the story proceeding without a RAPIDAPI_KEY prerequisite gate, and (b) consciously accept that SKY-002 implementation may build on inferred (not observed) FlightResult field mappings if only 429 responses are obtained.

stories.title: Implement typed Skyscanner API client with unit tests
stories.description: Create src/skyscanner/client.ts that wraps the Skyscanner RapidAPI and write src/skyscanner/client.test.ts in the same story. The client must export SkyscannerClient, SearchParams, and FlightResult. It must use the global fetch exclusively, validate inputs, sanitize the API key, handle HTTP errors, malformed responses, pagination (header-based), and unexpected runtime errors. Tests must use vi.stubGlobal for fetch mocking with afterEach vi.unstubAllGlobals(). Both tsc --noEmit and vitest run must exit 0 before the story is marked complete.
acceptanceCriteria: src/skyscanner/client.ts exports a SkyscannerClient class whose constructor signature is exactly: constructor({ apiKey }: { apiKey?: string })
SearchParams interface is exported from client.ts with exactly these fields: origin: string, destination: string, date: string, adults?: number — no additional required fields

FlightResult interface is exported from client.ts with exactly these fields: price: number, currency: string, airline: string, departure: string, arrival: string, duration: number, stops: number — no additional required fields
searchFlights uses the Node.js global fetch exclusively — no axios, node-fetch, got, or any other HTTP library is imported in client.ts
Every fetch call in searchFlights includes a 'User-Agent' header in the request headers object

When no apiKey is passed to the constructor and the RAPIDAPI_KEY environment variable is unset or empty, constructing SkyscannerClient throws an Error whose message references the missing key (e.g. contains 'API key')
When apiKey is passed as an empty string ('') to the constructor, SkyscannerClient throws the same missing-key Error as when apiKey is omitted entirely
When RAPIDAPI_KEY is set to an empty string in the environment and no apiKey is provided to the constructor, SkyscannerClient throws the missing-key Error
When an apiKey is provided to the constructor and RAPIDAPI_KEY is also set in the environment, the constructor-provided apiKey takes precedence over the environment variable

The constructor sanitizes the resolved apiKey value using the regex /^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$/ (allowing alphanumeric characters, underscores, and hyphens); if the key does not match, the constructor throws an Error indicating an invalid API key format
The apiKey is stored as a private field (using the private keyword or # prefix) on the SkyscannerClient instance and is not publicly accessible

searchFlights validates the date parameter against the regex /^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/ inline (no separate isValidDate helper function); if the format is invalid, searchFlights throws a descriptive Error before making any network call
When the API returns a 4xx or 5xx HTTP status, searchFlights rejects with an Error whose message includes the numeric HTTP status code
The Error thrown by searchFlights on HTTP 4xx/5xx does not include the apiKey value anywhere in its message string
The Error thrown by searchFlights on HTTP 4xx/5xx does not include the full request URL in its message string (to prevent leaking query parameters or other sensitive data)

When the API response body is not a plain array (Array.isArray(data) === false) or is missing any of the seven required FlightResult fields (price, currency, airline, departure, arrival, duration, stops) on any element, searchFlights rejects with a descriptive parse/validation Error

searchFlights checks the response header 'x-next-page' via res.headers?.get?.('x-next-page') to determine if pagination is needed; if the header is present and non-null, the client fetches subsequent pages and concatenates results before resolving

The pagination loop in searchFlights includes a termination guard (e.g., a maximum page count or a check that the next-page URL differs from the current URL) to prevent infinite loops if the server repeatedly returns the same next-page header value

Unexpected runtime errors caught in the catch block of searchFlights that are not already SkyscannerClient-originated errors are re-thrown wrapped in a new Error whose message matches /unexpected|runtime/i

SkyscannerClient-originated errors (constructor validation errors, date validation errors, HTTP errors, parse errors) are NOT re-wrapped by the runtime error catch block — they propagate with their original message intact

When fetch itself rejects (e.g., network timeout, DNS failure — the Promise returned by fetch rejects rather than resolving with a non-ok response), searchFlights rejects with an Error whose message matches /unexpected|runtime/i

When adults is omitted from SearchParams, searchFlights constructs the fetch URL without an 'adults' query parameter (or uses a documented default value) — the behavior must be deterministic and not produce 'undefined' in the URL string
src/skyscanner/client.test.ts contains at least 6 vitest tests using vi.stubGlobal('fetch', ...) for mocking, with afterEach(() => { vi.unstubAllGlobals(); }) — vi.spyOn is not used for fetch

Every vi.stubGlobal fetch mock in client.test.ts returns an object with all four fields: ok, status, json (async function), and headers: { get: () => null } — absence of headers will cause a TypeError on the pagination check
The fetch stub used in success-path tests returns a plain array (not a wrapped object) as the resolved value of json(), matching the Array.isArray check in the client
client.test.ts test (a): verifies the correct RapidAPI URL is constructed from SearchParams fields and that request headers include the API key and User-Agent
client.test.ts test (b): verifies a successful response body (plain array of FlightResult-shaped objects) is parsed and returned as FlightResult[]
client.test.ts test (c): verifies that a fetch response with ok=false and status=4xx causes searchFlights to reject with an Error whose message contains the status code

stories.title: Implement flight search CLI entry point with formatted table output
stories.description: Create `src/cli.ts` — a standalone Node entry point that accepts flight search arguments via `process.argv` and prints results as an aligned table. Parse flags manually (no commander, no yargs, zero new runtime deps). Require `RAPIDAPI_KEY` env var; exit 1 with a human-readable message if absent. Instantiate `SkyscannerClient` from `src/skyscanner-client.ts` (SKY-002), call `searchFlights` forwarding all parsed arguments including adults count, and render results in a dynamically-padded table with columns in this fixed order: Airline | Price | Departure | Arrival | Duration | Stops. Columns are delimited by ` | ` (space-pipe-space). Column widths are determined by the widest value in each column (including the header). A separator row of hyphens must appear between the header and data rows; each column's separator segment contains exactly as many hyphens as that column's padded width, with segments joined by ` | `. Price is right-aligned and prefixed with the currency symbol returned by the API (default `£` if absent); all other columns are left-aligned. If no flights are returned print `No flights found.` and exit 0. On any thrown error print the message to stderr and exit 1. Create `src/cli.test.ts` covering argument validation, successful render, empty-result render, missing env var, and error handling using vitest with `SkyscannerClient` mocked at the module boundary. The compiled output must be invokable as `node dist/cli.js ...` after `tsc`; `tsconfig.json` must have `outDir` set to `dist` and emit CommonJS-compatible output.

`tsconfig.json` sets `outDir` to `dist` and emits a module format compatible with `node dist/cli.js` invocation (CommonJS or ESM with `.mjs` extension consistently applied); after running `tsc`, `node dist/cli.js --help` or `node dist/cli.js` exits without a module-resolution or syntax error

stories.title: Flight result table renderer with dynamic alignment, padding, and separator row
stories.description: Create `src/table.ts` exporting a `renderTable(flights: Flight[], currency?: string): string` function. Render columns in fixed order: Airline | Price | Departure | Arrival | Duration | Stops. Cells are joined by the inter-column delimiter ` | ` (space-pipe-space); there is no leading or trailing pipe on any row. Column widths are computed dynamically: for every non-Price column, width W = Math.max(header.length, max data value length); for the Price column, each value is first formatted as `<symbol><numericValue>` and W = Math.max('Price'.length, max formatted price length). The separator row uses exactly W hyphens per column joined by ` | `. Price cells are right-aligned (leading spaces); all other cells are left-aligned (trailing spaces). Currency symbol defaults to `£` when the argument is absent, undefined, null, or empty string. Empty array input returns the exact string `No flights found.`. Wire `renderTable` into `src/cli.ts` (from SKY-003a); print the result to stdout via a single console.log or process.stdout.write call. CRITICAL: `src/cli.test.ts` already exists — do NOT regenerate it. Only write `src/table.ts` (and `src/types.ts` if needed). The implementation must satisfy the assertions in the existing test file.
acceptanceCriteria: `src/table.ts` exists, exports `renderTable(flights: Flight[], currency?: string): string`, imports the `Flight` type from the existing types module (from SKY-002) without redeclaring it, and `tsc --noEmit` reports zero errors

Header row columns appear in exactly this order: `Airline`, `Price`, `Departure`, `Arrival`, `Duration`, `Stops`; cells are joined by the delimiter ` | ` (one space, pipe, one space); the row has no leading and no trailing `|`

For every column except Price the computed column width W equals `Math.max(header.length, max(formattedValue.length for all rows))`; each data value is converted to string via `.toString()` before length comparison — this applies to all non-Price fields including numeric fields such as `stops`; no locale-aware formatting is applied

For the Price column each data cell is formatted as `<currencySymbol><numericValue>` where the numeric value is rendered exclusively via its plain `.toString()` method (no `toFixed`, no `toLocaleString`, no thousands separators, no forced decimal places); the computed width W equals `Math.max('Price'.length, max(formattedPrice.length for all rows))` so the symbol length and any multi-character currency symbol (e.g. `'USD'`) contributes to W

The separator row contains exactly one segment per column in the same column order; each segment is exactly W hyphens (using each column's computed W) with no spaces inside the segment; segments are joined by ` | ` (space-pipe-space), matching the inter-column delimiter used in header and data rows — no leading or trailing `|`; the separator row contains exactly 6 segments
All columns except Price are left-aligned: each cell value (header and data) is padded with trailing spaces until its length equals W for that column; no leading spaces are added to non-Price cells

Price column is right-aligned: each formatted price string (`<symbol><value>`) is padded with leading spaces until its length equals W; the header label `Price` is also padded with leading spaces to width W; no trailing spaces are added to Price cells

When the `currency` argument is a non-empty string it is used verbatim as the currency symbol prepended to the numeric price (including multi-character symbols such as `'USD'` or `'EUR'`); when `currency` is absent, `undefined`, `null`, or an empty string `''` the symbol defaults to `£`; a `price` value of `0` must render as `<symbol>0` and must not be treated as falsy

`renderTable([])` (empty array) returns the exact string `'No flights found.'` (strict equality, length 17, U+000A-free, no leading or trailing whitespace) as the function's return value — no header row, no separator row, no data rows

The returned string for non-empty input is the header row, separator row, and one data row per flight joined by `\n` (U+000A, LF — not CRLF) with no leading newline and no trailing newline in the returned value itself; splitting the returned string by `\n` must yield exactly `2 + flights.length` elements

`src/cli.ts` passes the `Flight[]` result of `searchFlights` and any `currency` CLI option to `renderTable`, then writes the returned string to stdout via a single `console.log` or `process.stdout.write` call; no additional formatting is applied to the returned string before writing

SkyscannerClient is instantiated inside each route handler (per-request), never at module level; no 503 middleware or RAPIDAPI_KEY environment variable check is added anywhere in server.ts

src/server.ts exports the Express app instance as a named or default export so that src/server.test.ts can import it without triggering the listen guard; the export must be present before the listen guard block

stories.title: Automated gate checks: Skyscanner mini-app review
stories.description: Execute the eleven automated gate checks (GATE-TS, GATE-TEST-EXIT, GATE-TEST-RESULTS, GATE-TEST-COVERAGE, GATE-SECRET, GATE-INPUT-400, GATE-ERROR-HANDLING, GATE-ASYNC-EXPRESS-ERROR, GATE-PATH-SAFETY, GATE-CONTENT-TYPE, GATE-DEPENDENCY-AUDIT, GATE-CORS) against /tmp/skyscanner-app and verify that each exits clean. The review-agent records results in /tmp/skyscanner-app/review/SKY-006-review.md and sets the Verdict token to PASS only when every sub-check passes. Depends on SKY-006-a producing the review scaffold and on SKY-001–SKY-005 delivering a complete implementation.
acceptanceCriteria: GATE-TS: Running `tsc --noEmit` from /tmp/skyscanner-app exits with code 0 and produces zero lines of diagnostic output on both stdout and stderr. tsconfig.json at the project root must contain `"strict": true` under `compilerOptions`. If the root tsconfig.json uses an `extends` field (directly or transitively), no file in that extends chain may set `"strict": false` or override any strict sub-flag (e.g. `noImplicitAny`, `strictNullChecks`) to `false`. The gate check must capture both stdout and stderr separately and record both in the review document; a non-empty stderr alone (even with exit code 0) is treated as a gate WARNING that must be explicitly noted.

GATE-TEST-EXIT + GATE-TEST-RESULTS: Running `npx vitest run` from /tmp/skyscanner-app exits with code 0 (any non-zero exit code is a gate failure). The vitest output reports 0 failed tests, 0 skipped tests, and 0 todo tests; at least 1 test must be reported as passed to prevent an empty suite from producing a false PASS. Tests inside `describe.skip`, `it.skip`, `test.skip`, or `test.todo` blocks count as skipped/incomplete and cause this gate to fail. No line/branch coverage floor is imposed by this story — a separate coverage-floor story should be opened if a floor is desired.

GATE-TEST-COVERAGE: At least one non-empty test file (*.test.ts or *.spec.ts) exists under each of the three implementation layers — client (e.g. src/client/ or equivalent), CLI (e.g. src/cli/ or equivalent), and server/routes (e.g. src/server/, src/routes/, or equivalent). Each such file must (a) be syntactically valid TypeScript, (b) contain at least one `it()` or `test()` call that is not inside a `.skip` block, and (c) not consist solely of type-import statements with no runtime assertions. Each test file is counted under exactly one layer (no double-counting). The layer directory examples are illustrative; any directory whose name or path unambiguously maps to one of the three concerns satisfies the criterion.

GATE-SECRET: A case-insensitive grep for the literal Skyscanner API key value across all files under src/, test/, dist/, build/, .next/, out/, any *.env* files (excluding *.env.example and *.env.template), any captured test-output artefacts, and package-lock.json / yarn.lock returns zero matches. The key must be sourced exclusively from a named environment variable (e.g. SKYSCANNER_API_KEY) at runtime. Additionally, .gitignore (or equivalent VCS ignore file) must contain an entry that excludes all *.env files that may carry secrets (excluding *.env.example and *.env.template) — absence of .gitignore or a missing exclusion entry is a gate failure. If a CI pipeline artefact store is present, the CI pipeline must mask the environment variable value in all log output, verified by the absence of the key literal in any stored CI log artefact; if no CI pipeline is configured for this project, this sub-check is marked N/A-PASS and that determination is documented in the review.

GATE-INPUT-400: Every Express route that declares a required parameter (path, query, or body) returns HTTP 400 with (a) the header `Content-Type: application/json` and (b) a JSON body matching `{ "error": string }` when the parameter is (i) absent, (ii) present but empty string, and (iii) present but of an invalid type. Each of these three sub-cases must be covered by at least one automated test in the test suite.

GATE-ERROR-HANDLING + GATE-ASYNC-EXPRESS-ERROR: Every outbound API call is enclosed in a try/catch (or equivalent .catch()) block. Non-2xx responses from upstream are surfaced as a JSON body `{ "error": string, "status": number }` with a matching HTTP status code; the original upstream 4xx–5xx status code must be preserved; if the upstream returns a status outside 400–599 (e.g. 1xx, 3xx without redirect-following, or a network-level error including connection timeout, DNS failure, or ECONNREFUSED) the server must respond with HTTP 502. Every async Express route handler must either (a) be wrapped in a try/catch that calls `next(err)` on failure, or (b) be wrapped by a utility (e.g. `asyncHandler`) that forwards thrown errors to Express's error-handling middleware — no async route handler may allow an unhandled promise rejection to propagate silently. At least one automated test must verify that an async route that throws internally returns a structured error response rather than hanging or crashing. At least one automated test must verify that a simulated network-level error (e.g. fetch rejection) produces an HTTP 502 response with the correct JSON body.

GATE-PATH-SAFETY: If the Express app performs manual static-file serving (i.e. any route reads from the filesystem in response to a user-supplied path, beyond what `express.static` provides internally): user-supplied path segments must be sanitised using `path.resolve` (to eliminate `../` sequences) and `fs.realpath` or equivalent (to dereference symlinks), and validated to confirm the fully-resolved real path starts with the hard-coded base directory constant before any file I/O is performed. A test must demonstrate that a `../` traversal attempt returns HTTP 400 or 403 without reading outside the base directory, and a second test must demonstrate that a symlink pointing outside the base directory is also rejected. If the app uses only `express.static` for all static-file serving and performs no additional manual filesystem reads on user-supplied paths, the symlink-resolution sub-check is marked N/A-PASS and only the `express.static` usage must be confirmed in the review document.

GATE-CONTENT-TYPE: Every Express route that returns a JSON response (including error responses) sets the `Content-Type` header to `application/json` or `application/json; charset=utf-8`. This is verified by at least one automated test per route group that asserts on the response Content-Type header value. If CORS is active (see GATE-CORS), the OPTIONS preflight response must also set appropriate `Content-Type` (or omit a body entirely — an empty-body 204 is acceptable); a preflight response that returns a non-JSON body with `Content-Type: application/json` is a gate failure.

GATE-DEPENDENCY-AUDIT: Running `npm audit --audit-level=high` from /tmp/skyscanner-app exits with code 0, indicating zero high-severity or critical-severity vulnerabilities in the dependency tree. Any audit failure is treated as a gate failure and its full output is quoted verbatim in the review document.

GATE-CORS: The Express app's CORS policy is reviewed for correctness. Specifically: (a) if the app sets `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`, this is flagged unless the app is explicitly documented as a public read-only API; (b) if the app uses the `cors` package or sets CORS headers manually, the allowed-origin list must be explicitly enumerated or derived from a validated environment variable — wildcard origins combined with `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true` must be treated as a gate failure; (c) at least one automated test asserts on the CORS headers returned by a representative route for a standard GET/POST request; (d) if CORS is active, at least one automated test must send an OPTIONS preflight request and assert that the response includes the correct `Access-Control-Allow-Methods` and `Access-Control-Allow-Headers` values. If the app serves no cross-origin clients and sets no CORS headers, this gate is marked N/A-PASS and that determination is documented in the review.

GATE-ENV-CONFIG: The application must validate all required environment variables at startup (before binding to a port or executing any business logic). If a required variable (e.g. SKYSCANNER_API_KEY) is absent or empty, the process must exit with a non-zero exit code and emit a human-readable error message to stderr identifying the missing variable by name. The application must NOT start successfully with a missing required environment variable and silently use an undefined/null value. At least one automated test (using environment-variable stubbing or process isolation) must verify that the application exits or throws on startup when a required variable is absent.

VERDICT: The review file /tmp/skyscanner-app/review/SKY-006-review.md must contain exactly one line of the form `Verdict: <TOKEN>` where `<TOKEN>` matches the regular expression `^(PASS|FAIL)$` exactly (no trailing whitespace, no extra characters, no duplicate Verdict lines — a file containing two or more `Verdict:` lines is itself a gate failure). The token is `PASS` if and only if all gates enumerated in the ARTEFACT AC pass (including any N/A-PASS gates); it is `FAIL` followed on subsequent lines by a Markdown bullet list of the identifiers of every failing gate otherwise.

ARTEFACT: /tmp/skyscanner-app/review/SKY-006-review.md must exist and be non-empty. It must contain one clearly labelled Markdown section per gate, using the gate identifier as the heading (## GATE-TS, ## GATE-TEST-EXIT + GATE-TEST-RESULTS, ## GATE-TEST-COVERAGE, ## GATE-SECRET, ## GATE-INPUT-400, ## GATE-ERROR-HANDLING + GATE-ASYNC-EXPRESS-ERROR, ## GATE-PATH-SAFETY, ## GATE-CONTENT-TYPE, ## GATE-DEPENDENCY-AUDIT, ## GATE-CORS, ## GATE-ENV-CONFIG — eleven sections total). Each section must record: (1) the exact command invoked (if applicable), (2) the command's exit code, (3) observed command output or evidence quoted verbatim in a fenced code block, and (4) the pass/fail/N/A-PASS status. The file's last-modified filesystem timestamp must be equal to or later than the timestamp of the most recent gate-check run, preventing a stale cached artefact from being used. VCS commit of this file is explicitly out of scope for this story.

stories.title: Prerequisite gate: verify SKY-001–SKY-005 outputs before review
stories.description: Isolates the dependency-checking step from the substantive code review. This story succeeds when the /tmp/skyscanner-app workspace is confirmed to be in a reviewable state (src/ tree present, package.json present, tsconfig.json present, all five prior stories marked complete in the tracker). On success it emits a machine-readable gate-passed signal that SKY-006-B depends on. On failure it emits a BLOCKED signal and halts the pipeline without creating a partial review document.
acceptanceCriteria: Before any other action, the agent verifies the existence of all four required paths in order: /tmp/skyscanner-app (directory), /tmp/skyscanner-app/src (directory), /tmp/skyscanner-app/package.json (file), and /tmp/skyscanner-app/tsconfig.json (file). Checks are performed sequentially and stop at the first missing path.

If the /tmp/skyscanner-app/review directory does not exist, the agent creates it (including any intermediate directories) before writing any output files, regardless of whether the gate passes or fails.

If any required path is absent, the agent writes exactly one line to /tmp/skyscanner-app/review/SKY-006-review.md in the format `BLOCKED: dependency <missing-path> not satisfied` (where <missing-path> is the first failing path), writes the identical message to stderr, and exits with code 1. No additional content is appended to the review document.

If all required paths are present, the agent writes a JSON file at /tmp/skyscanner-app/review/.gate-passed.json containing exactly the keys `story` (string, value `"SKY-006-A"`), `timestamp` (string, ISO-8601 UTC format), and `status` (string, value `"passed"`), then exits with code 0. No other keys are written to this file.

The gate check is idempotent: executing it multiple times against a fully valid workspace always exits with code 0 and overwrites /tmp/skyscanner-app/review/.gate-passed.json with an updated timestamp on each run, without duplicating or appending content.

The agent does not write any content to /tmp/skyscanner-app/review/SKY-006-review.md when the gate passes; that file is reserved exclusively for failure output and subsequent review content written by SKY-006-B.

All filesystem errors (e.g. permission denied when creating the review directory or writing output files) are caught, reported to stderr with a descriptive message prefixed `ERROR:`, and cause the agent to exit with code 2 to distinguish infrastructure failures from dependency failures.
The agent produces no stdout output under any execution path; all human-readable messaging is directed exclusively to stderr.

stories.title: Execute and document Skyscanner mini-app code review
stories.description: Performs the substantive five-category code review (TypeScript, Tests, Security, Error Handling, Express Safety) against the Skyscanner mini-app source and produces the final review document at /tmp/skyscanner-app/review/SKY-006-review.md. Execution is gated on SKY-006-A having written /tmp/skyscanner-app/review/.gate-passed.json with status 'passed'. This story owns all tool invocations, finding recording, Verdict determination, and exit-code signalling for CI.
acceptanceCriteria: Before executing any review step the agent reads /tmp/skyscanner-app/review/.gate-passed.json; if the file is absent, unreadable, or does not contain the key-value pair '"status": "passed"' the agent halts immediately, emits a dependency error message that identifies the missing or invalid gate file by path, and exits with code 2 (distinct from exit code 1 used for a FAIL verdict); additionally, if the file is present and readable but is not valid JSON the agent treats this as an invalid gate file and exits with code 2, emitting a parse-error message that includes the file path and the JSON parse error description.

The agent performs a TypeScript category review: it inspects all .ts source files for strict-mode compliance, absence of untyped 'any' escape-hatches, correct interface/type usage, and absence of compiler errors reported by tsc --noEmit; every finding is recorded as a structured entry containing: file path (relative to /tmp/skyscanner-app), line number (a positive integer ≥ 1), severity (ERROR | WARN | INFO), gate name (e.g. TS_STRICT, TS_NO_ANY, TS_COMPILER_ERROR), and a one-sentence rationale; if a source file cannot be read due to permissions or I/O error the agent records a single ERROR-severity finding with gate name TS_FILE_UNREADABLE for that file and continues reviewing remaining files.

The agent performs a Tests category review: it verifies that a test suite exists and is executable, and that line-coverage meets or exceeds the target floor — the floor is the value declared in the project README or package.json (e.g. jest coverageThreshold.global.lines); if the project declares a branch or statement threshold instead of a line threshold, that declared metric and value is used as the floor; if no target is declared the default floor is 80% line coverage; it also verifies that test files follow the project's naming and co-location conventions; every finding is recorded with the same schema as AC-2, using gate names such as TEST_SUITE_EXISTS, TEST_COVERAGE_FLOOR, TEST_NAMING_CONVENTION.

The agent performs a Security category review: it checks for hard-coded secrets or credentials (gate SECURITY_NO_HARDCODED_SECRETS), unsafe use of eval or the Function constructor (gate SECURITY_NO_EVAL), dependency versions with known CVEs using available lock-file data (gate SECURITY_DEPENDENCY_CVE), and missing input sanitisation on user-supplied data (gate SECURITY_INPUT_SANITISATION); every finding is recorded with the same schema as AC-2.

The agent performs an Error Handling category review: it verifies that all async operations have explicit catch paths or are wrapped in try/catch (gate EH_ASYNC_CATCH), that error responses never leak stack traces or internal paths to HTTP clients (gate EH_NO_STACK_LEAK), that unhandled-rejection and uncaughtException process-level handlers are present (gate EH_PROCESS_HANDLERS), and that async Express route handlers do not throw without forwarding the error via next(err) (gate EH_EXPRESS_NEXT_ERR — a handler is non-compliant if it contains an await expression or returns a Promise and does not wrap its body in try/catch with a next(err) call in the catch block); every finding is recorded with the same schema as AC-2.

The agent performs an Express Safety category review: it checks for helmet or equivalent security-header middleware (gate EXPRESS_HELMET), rate-limiting middleware on public endpoints (gate EXPRESS_RATE_LIMIT), absence of directory-traversal vectors in static-file serving or path construction (gate EXPRESS_NO_PATH_TRAVERSAL), and CORS configuration (gate EXPRESS_CORS — PASS when cors() is called with an explicit origin allowlist or when CORS is intentionally disabled and a comment documents the rationale; FAIL when cors() is called with origin: '*' on a non-public API, when no CORS middleware is present on routes that accept cross-origin requests, or when the origin value is derived from an unsanitised request header); every finding is recorded with the same schema as AC-2.

The review document written to /tmp/skyscanner-app/review/SKY-006-review.md contains exactly eight top-level sections in this order: (1) Executive Summary, (2) Scope & Methodology, (3) TypeScript Review, (4) Tests Review, (5) Security Review, (6) Error Handling Review, (7) Express Safety Review, (8) Verdict — each section heading formatted as a level-2 Markdown heading (## ).

The Verdict section must have ^(PASS|FAIL)$ as its first non-blank line (the token alone, no other text on that line); subsequent lines provide a concise rationale; Verdict is PASS only when zero ERROR-severity findings exist across all five categories, otherwise Verdict is FAIL.

The Executive Summary section includes: total finding counts broken down by category and by severity (ERROR / WARN / INFO), the overall Verdict token (PASS or FAIL), and the UTC timestamp at which the review completed in ISO-8601 format (e.g. 2024-06-01T12:34:56Z) with second-level precision and explicit 'Z' suffix.

The agent exits with code 0 when Verdict is PASS and with code 1 when Verdict is FAIL, allowing CI pipelines to gate on the exit code without parsing the document; exit code 2 is reserved exclusively for the gate-prerequisite failure described in AC-1; if the review document cannot be written to disk (e.g. directory does not exist, insufficient permissions, disk full) the agent emits an I/O error message identifying the target path and the OS error, and exits with code 3 (distinct from codes 0, 1, and 2).

The review document is valid UTF-8 Markdown, contains no placeholder text (i.e. the literal strings 'TODO', 'TBD', 'FIXME', or 'N/A' used as a substitute for genuine analysis, or any section body that consists solely of whitespace), and every finding count stated in the Executive Summary is traceable to a corresponding named finding entry (identified by gate name, file path, and line number) in its respective category section; each finding entry must have a composite identifier (gate name + file path + line number) that is unique within the document — duplicate entries for the same location and gate are not permitted.

The document write operation is atomic from the reader's perspective: the agent writes the complete review content to a temporary file in the same directory (e.g. SKY-006-review.md.tmp) and renames it to the final path only after the write is fully flushed; if a previous run's output file already exists at the final path it is overwritten by the rename without leaving a partially written file.

When the agent encounters a source file that matches the *.ts glob but is not valid UTF-8 text (e.g. a binary file with a .ts extension), it records a single WARN-severity finding with gate name TS_FILE_ENCODING_INVALID for that file, skips static analysis of that file, and continues processing remaining files; this behaviour is verified by confirming the finding appears in the TypeScript Review section and the file is not listed as analysed.

All five category review sections (TypeScript, Tests, Security, Error Handling, Express Safety) must each contain at least one finding entry — either a genuine finding or an explicit INFO-severity 'no issues found' entry using the gate name <CATEGORY>_NO_ISSUES (e.g. TS_NO_ISSUES) — so that no section body is empty; a section that contains only a heading with no finding entries is treated as a placeholder and fails the AC-11 placeholder check.

The agent must not write any data to stdout or stderr that reveals the contents of environment variables, internal file paths outside /tmp/skyscanner-app, or process credentials; all diagnostic messages emitted to stderr are limited to: the gate-file error (AC-1), the I/O error (AC-10), and per-category progress indicators that contain only the category name and file count.

stories.title: Code review (Part A): Prerequisites, document structure, TypeScript, and test checks
stories.description: First half of the Skyscanner mini-app code review. The agent verifies that all prerequisite stories are satisfied, creates the review document with the correct six-section structure, runs the TypeScript compiler, and verifies test execution and per-layer test coverage. Output is written to /tmp/skyscanner-app/review/SKY-006-review.md. This story must be completed before SKY-006-B begins.
acceptanceCriteria: PREREQUISITE GATE — Before any review step executes the agent MUST verify: (a) the directory /tmp/skyscanner-app exists, (b) a src/ subtree is present beneath it containing at least one TypeScript source file (*.ts or *.tsx), and (c) a package.json is present at /tmp/skyscanner-app/package.json. If any of these three conditions is not met the agent MUST immediately write a single-line file at /tmp/skyscanner-app/review/SKY-006-review.md containing exactly `BLOCKED: dependency SKY-00N not satisfied` (where N identifies the first unsatisfied story by its numeric suffix), emit the same message to stderr, exit with a non-zero code, and produce NO further review content. Any partial review document written after a failed prerequisite check is itself treated as a review failure.

The file /tmp/skyscanner-app/review/SKY-006-review.md MUST be created (parent directory /tmp/skyscanner-app/review/ created if absent) and MUST contain all six required sections with exact H2 headings in this order and no other H2 headings: `## TypeScript`, `## Tests`, `## Security`, `## Error Handling`, `## Express Safety`, `## Verdict`. Any missing heading, any heading with different casing or punctuation (e.g. `## Typescript` or `## TypeScript:` are both non-conforming), or any additional H2 heading anywhere in the document is a blocking structural finding that forces Verdict: FAIL.

A 'blocking finding' is defined as any discrete defect, failed check, or policy violation discovered during live inspection that, if left unresolved, would prevent the mini-app from meeting its stated requirements. Each blocking finding MUST be recorded as a numbered list item under the relevant category section and MUST include all four of the following fields: (1) the relative file path (relative to /tmp/skyscanner-app), (2) the line number or line range where the issue was observed, (3) a one-sentence description of the defect, and (4) the specific acceptance criterion or policy it violates. A finding that omits any of these four fields is itself considered incomplete, and the category containing it is treated as having an unresolved blocking finding.

Each of the five category sections (TypeScript, Tests, Security, Error Handling, Express Safety) MUST reference at least one concrete relative file path or specific line-number finding discovered during live inspection of the actual codebase at /tmp/skyscanner-app. Content that could have been produced without reading the actual source files (boilerplate, placeholder sentences, generic advice) constitutes a blocking structural finding for that section. For every finding the agent MUST record the exact tool invocation used to produce it (command run, exit code, and output truncated to 500 characters if longer) as a fenced code block immediately following the finding list item.

TypeScript check: The agent MUST run `tsc --noEmit --project /tmp/skyscanner-app/tsconfig.json` and capture stdout, stderr, and exit code. Before running, the agent MUST read /tmp/skyscanner-app/tsconfig.json and confirm that `"strict": true` appears in the top-level `compilerOptions` object of that file (not solely inherited via an `extends` chain without being re-stated); if it is absent, that absence is itself a blocking TypeScript finding recorded before the compiler is invoked. The tsc command MUST exit with code 0 and produce zero bytes on both stdout and stderr; any non-zero exit code or any diagnostic line on either stream is a blocking TypeScript finding. The raw command output (or a truncation to 2000 characters with a truncation notice) MUST be reproduced verbatim in the `## TypeScript` section.

Tests check — execution: The agent MUST read /tmp/skyscanner-app/package.json, extract the value of `scripts.test`, and run that exact command from the /tmp/skyscanner-app working directory (falling back to `npx vitest run` only if the `test` key is absent or empty). The agent MUST capture stdout, stderr, and exit code. The command MUST exit with code 0. The Vitest (or equivalent runner) summary line MUST report 0 failed, 0 skipped, and 0 todo tests. Any non-zero exit code or any non-zero value in failed/skipped/todo counts is a blocking Tests finding. The raw summary output (last 2000 characters of combined stdout+stderr, with a truncation notice if trimmed) MUST be reproduced verbatim in the `## Tests` section.

Tests check — coverage by layer: At least one non-empty test file (containing at least one `it(`, `test(`, or `describe(` call) MUST be present for each of the following three layers: (a) Skyscanner API client — a file matching the glob `src/**/*.client.test.*` OR any file under src/ whose base name (without extension) contains both a word identifying the Skyscanner client module (e.g. 'client', 'skyscanner', 'api') and either 'test' or 'spec'; (b) CLI entry-point — any file under src/ whose base name contains a word identifying the CLI or bin module (e.g. 'cli', 'bin', 'index') and either 'test' or 'spec'; (c) Express server/router — any file under src/ whose base name contains a word identifying the server or router module (e.g. 'server', 'router', 'app') and either 'test' or 'spec'. Absence of a qualifying non-empty file for any single layer is a blocking Tests finding. The agent MUST list the resolved absolute path of each qualifying test file found in the `## Tests` section.

Upon completing all checks assigned to this story the agent MUST leave the review document in a consistent intermediate state: the `## TypeScript` and `## Tests` sections MUST be fully populated with findings and verbatim tool output as specified above; the remaining four sections (`## Security`, `## Error Handling`, `## Express Safety`, `## Verdict`) MUST be present as H2 headings with no content beneath them (not even a blank placeholder line containing text). The document MUST NOT contain any line beginning with `Verdict:` or any text beneath the `## Verdict` heading until SKY-006-B writes it. Writing a Verdict line or populating the Security, Error Handling, or Express Safety sections in SKY-006-A is itself a blocking structural finding.

stories.title: Code review (Part B): Security, error handling, Express safety, and verdict
stories.description: Second half of the Skyscanner mini-app code review. The agent reads the partially-populated review document produced by SKY-006-A and performs deep inspection of security (API key exposure and query-parameter validation), error handling (missing-param 400 responses and upstream error propagation), and Express static-file safety (path traversal prevention). It then writes the `## Verdict` section and finalises the document. This story depends on SKY-006-A being complete.
acceptanceCriteria: Security check — API key exposure: The agent MUST determine the exact string value assigned to the API key (from environment variable, config constant, or .env file under /tmp/skyscanner-app) and perform a case-insensitive literal grep for that value across: (a) all files under src/, (b) the captured stdout/stderr from the `vitest run` execution, and (c) any .log files under /tmp/skyscanner-app. Zero matches MUST be found across all three scopes; any match is a blocking Security finding. If the API key value cannot be determined (e.g. it is only read from process.env at runtime with no default), the agent MUST record this as an informational note and instead grep for the environment variable name to confirm it is never interpolated into a response body or log statement.

Security check — query parameter validation: Every Express route handler that accepts query parameters MUST validate each parameter before use. Validation MUST occur via an explicit check (e.g. `if (!req.query.x)` or equivalent), a validation library schema (e.g. Zod, Joi, express-validator), or dedicated middleware — implicit type coercion alone is insufficient. The agent MUST enumerate all route handlers found in src/ and confirm each one validates its inputs. Any route handler that uses a query parameter without prior explicit validation is a blocking Security finding.

Error Handling check — missing/invalid parameters: Every Express route handler that declares a required query parameter MUST return HTTP 400 with a JSON body of the shape `{ "error": "<non-empty string>" }` (additional fields are permitted) when that parameter is: (a) absent from the request, (b) present but an empty string, or (c) present but not parseable as its declared type (e.g. a non-numeric string where a number is required). The agent MUST verify this by static analysis of the handler code and, where the test suite exercises these paths, by inspecting the relevant test assertions. Failure of any sub-case (a), (b), or (c) for any route is a blocking Error Handling finding.

Error Handling check — upstream error propagation: All code paths that invoke or await the upstream Skyscanner API MUST be wrapped in try/catch or .catch() / Promise rejection handling. Non-2xx HTTP status codes returned by the upstream MUST be mapped to a JSON response of the shape `{ "error": string, "status": number }` forwarded to the Express caller with the same HTTP status code or a semantically equivalent one (e.g. 502 Bad Gateway is acceptable for a 500 upstream). No unhandled-rejection or uncaught-exception path reachable via upstream errors is permitted. The agent MUST trace every call site to the upstream API in src/ and confirm coverage; any unguarded call site or missing non-2xx mapping is a blocking Error Handling finding.

Express Safety check — path traversal prevention: Static file serving MUST use `express.static` with a base directory derived exclusively from a fixed, hard-coded constant (e.g. `path.join(__dirname, 'public')` or `path.resolve(__dirname, '../public')`). No user-controlled input — including but not limited to query parameters, request headers, URL path segments, or body fields — MAY be concatenated, interpolated, or passed as an argument into `__dirname`, `process.cwd()`, `path.resolve()`, `path.join()`, `fs.readFile()`, or any other file-system call used to derive the path of a served or read file. The agent MUST grep src/ for all occurrences of the following tokens: `path.join`, `path.resolve`, `readFile`, `createReadStream`, and `sendFile`, and inspect each call site. Any call site that incorporates user-controlled input is a blocking Express Safety finding.

Verdict integrity: The `## Verdict` section MUST contain exactly one line matching the POSIX ERE regex `^(PASS|FAIL)$` (case-sensitive, anchored at both start and end of line, no leading or trailing whitespace, no punctuation, no markdown formatting). If the Verdict is FAIL, a prioritised numbered list of ALL blocking findings across all categories MUST follow immediately under the heading — with no intervening blank line or sub-heading — with each item cross-referencing its category name and the AC number it violates. The Verdict MUST be PASS if and only if all category checks produced zero blocking findings. A PASS verdict with any recorded blocking finding, or a FAIL verdict with no recorded blocking findings, is itself a review failure and the document MUST be regenerated from the point of the Verdict section.

Tool exit code authority: Before writing the Verdict line, the agent MUST collate all tool invocations across both SKY-006-A and SKY-006-B and record any that exited with a non-zero code. If any such non-zero exit code exists, the Verdict MUST be FAIL regardless of the narrative content of the category sections. The collated list of non-zero exit codes and the commands that produced them MUST appear as an appended sub-list under the first FAIL finding (or as a standalone finding if no other blocking findings were recorded), labelled `Tool Exit Code Failures`.

Document finalisation and atomic write: Upon writing the Verdict line the agent MUST perform a self-check verifying: (i) the final document satisfies all structural constraints from SKY-006-A AC-2 (exactly six H2 headings in the required order, no extra headings), and (ii) every blocking finding recorded in any section is represented in the Verdict's consolidated numbered list (if Verdict is FAIL). A document that passes this self-check MUST be written atomically — first to a uniquely-named temp file under /tmp/skyscanner-app/review/ (e.g. `SKY-006-review.md.tmp.<pid>`), then renamed to `/tmp/skyscanner-app/review/SKY-006-review.md` — to prevent partial reads by downstream tooling. If the self-check fails, the agent MUST correct the document before performing the atomic write. If `/tmp/skyscanner-app/review/SKY-006-review.md` already exists from a prior run, it MUST be fully overwritten (not appended to) by the atomic rename; the agent MUST NOT open the existing file in append mode at any point.

Dependency-guard precondition: Before performing any category check, the agent MUST verify that `/tmp/skyscanner-app/review/SKY-006-review.md` exists and contains the five H2 section headings expected from SKY-006-A (i.e. `## Project Structure`, `## Dependencies`, `## Code Quality`, `## Test Coverage`, and `## Security` at minimum — exact heading names are defined by SKY-006-A AC-2). If the file is absent, empty, or missing any required heading, the agent MUST abort with a non-zero exit code and emit a human-readable error message identifying the missing prerequisite; it MUST NOT create a partial or blank review document in this failure mode.

JSON error response Content-Type enforcement: Every Express route handler that returns an error response (HTTP 4xx or 5xx) with a JSON body MUST set the `Content-Type` response header to `application/json` (or `application/json; charset=utf-8`). The agent MUST verify this by static analysis — confirming that either `res.json(...)` is used (which sets Content-Type automatically in Express), or `res.setHeader('Content-Type', 'application/json')` / `res.type('json')` is called before `res.send(...)`. Any error response path that sends a JSON-shaped body without an explicit or implicit `application/json` Content-Type is a blocking Error Handling finding.

Supply-chain secrets check: The agent MUST inspect the resolved contents of `node_modules/` (or, if node_modules is absent, the lockfile at `/tmp/skyscanner-app/package-lock.json` or `yarn.lock`) for any file whose name matches `*.env`, `.env*`, `config.json`, or `secrets.*` at depth ≤ 2 within any single package directory. Each such file MUST be scanned for the API key value (if known) and for common credential patterns (bare 32+-character hex strings, strings matching `sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}`, or strings matching `Bearer [A-Za-z0-9+/=]{20,}`). Any match is a blocking Security finding labelled `Supply-Chain Credential Exposure`. If node_modules is absent and no lockfile exists, the agent MUST record this as an informational note and skip this check without issuing a finding.
